Sarecycline and P-gp inhibitors: Sarecycline can increase the levels or effects of drugs like voxilaprevir, abemaciclib, afatinib, aliskiren, ambrisentan, amiodarone, amitriptyline, apixaban, atorvastatin, bendamustine, betrixaban, brentuximab vedotin, budesonide, carvedilol, ceritinib, cetirizine, crizotinib, cyclosporine, dabigatran, dabrafenib, dasabuvir, daunorubicin, desloratadine, dexamethasone, digoxin, diltiazem, docetaxel, doxorubicin, duvelisib, edoxaban, eletriptan, erythromycin (various forms), everolimus, fexofenadine, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, hydrocortisone, idarubicin, imatinib, indinavir, and others by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. This can lead to increased drug toxicity. Close monitoring is recommended, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. 2. Sarecycline and zinc: Zinc can decrease the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline by binding to it in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. To minimize this interaction, separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 3. Sarecycline and aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate: These substances can reduce the absorption of sarecycline in the GI tract, potentially decreasing its effectiveness. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and dosing should be separated to avoid reduced efficacy. 4. Sarecycline and multivalent cation-containing products: Products containing multivalent cations, such as calcium, magnesium, aluminum, or iron, can impair the absorption of tetracyclines, including sarecycline, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products and monitor closely. 5. Sarecycline and oral retinoids (e.g., acitretin, bexarotene): Concomitant use of oral retinoids with tetracyclines can increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (intracranial hypertension). This combination is contraindicated. 6. Sarecycline and penicillins (e.g., amoxicillin, ampicillin, dicloxacillin): Tetracyclines, including sarecycline, may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid using these drugs together, or consider alternative therapies. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if co-administered. 7. Sarecycline and cholera vaccine: Systemic antibiotics, including sarecycline, may inactivate the live cholera vaccine strain, reducing its effectiveness. Avoid administering the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 8. Sarecycline and bile acid sequestrants (e.g., cholestyramine, colesevelam, colestipol): These agents can reduce the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor for decreased effects of tetracyclines. 9. Sarecycline and iron-containing products (e.g., ferrous sulfate, ferric citrate, ferric gluconate): Iron products can inhibit the absorption of sarecycline in the GI tract, reducing its efficacy. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy, separate dosing, and monitor closely. 10. Sarecycline and atracurium/cisatracurium: Sarecycline may enhance the effects of these neuromuscular blocking agents through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely for respiratory complications. 11.
